Duration: ~49 minutes

Transcript:
00:00 Lena: All right, thanks everyone for joining, um this is Lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is Marcus our solutions engineer. Priya, Tom, Sofia, thanks for taking the time. Can you just confirm you can hear us?
00:10 Priya: Yep we can hear you, thanks Lena. Sitting in SF so timing's good.
00:18 Tom: Hi, Tom here. CTO at EmberCare. We're exploring a few options to add LLM features in product triage and summarization.
00:25 Marcus: Hey team, quick note—i'll do most of the technical bits later. For today we're hoping to understand your goals and get you to a first-token using Redwood hosted API as fast as possible.
00:38 Priya: Perfect. Our main priorities are speed to shipping (PLG flows), low friction for product, and then security/compliance is a gating factor for production. Initially we want to run a pilot on de-identified clinical notes, possibly PHI later.
00:52 Lena: Got it. So we'll cover hosted quickstart and what Dedicated/Private would add for PHI. Also we'll point you to our free credits and onboarding time estimates.
01:05 Sofia: Quick question—what do folks usually need to get a first token? Like SDK key, sample prompts, and how long?
01:14 Marcus: Typically, if you sign up self-serve, you can get an API key, install the SDK, and hit /completions in under an hour. With our quickstart templates product engineers often get to first-token in 10-30 minutes. There are a few nuances—CORS, CI secrets, and if you want streaming we have examples.
01:34 Tom: And latency? We care about median latency under 300ms for short prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?
01:41 Marcus: For short prompts on our hosted endpoints in us-west region, sub-300ms is achievable on smaller models; with batching or longer sequences latency increases. We also have Dedicated reserved pools if you need consistent p99s.
01:56 Priya: We're trying to decide between hosted for quick iteration vs dedicated/private for compliance. What does Private entail?
02:06 Lena: Private is our VPC or on-prem option—control plane is customer-managed, we support SAML SSO, KMS integrations, and audit logs. There's more setup time and an enterprise contract, but it's needed for PHI/regulatory workloads.
02:20 Priya: Do you support HSM or customer HSM-backed KMS?
02:24 Marcus: Yes, we integrate with cloud KMS and can support HSM-backed keys depending on the deployment pattern. There are a few onboarding steps, cert installs, and network peering.
02:36 Tom: Good. On costs—what's the best way to reason about cost for early pilot? Per-token hosted plus burst capacity?
02:45 Lena: Usually customers start with hosted usage (pay-as-you-go), use free credits to validate usage. If predictable volume follows, move to Dedicated reserved capacity which we price as monthly commits plus usage for bursts. Marcus can run a quick cost projection once you share expected tokens/seq lengths.
03:03 Sofia: We have two main flows: short triage prompts (~50 tokens) and summarization (~800-1,200 tokens). We can provide sample corpus.
03:11 Marcus: That's perfect. For token economics that mix suggests hybrid: hosted to validate, then Dedicated for heavy summarization to bring unit cost down. Also, caching prefix responses can save tokens on repeated prompts.
03:27 Priya: About security docs—do you have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts?
03:31 Lena: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestation, and a security pack including pen test summaries, data flow diagrams. We'll share the security questionnaire.
03:41 Tom: What's the SLAs on hosted vs Dedicated?
03:45 Lena: Hosted has best-effort with published latency profiles; Dedicated is SLA-backed for uptime and latency targets as part of the reserved contract. Private gets bespoke SLAs.
03:56 Priya: Any gotchas for self-serve onboarding? We want product folks to try without needing infra.
04:03 Marcus: Self-serve is smooth—sign up, get credits, a dashboard with request logs, and SDKs. Common friction points are network policies (CORS) and firewall rules when integrating from web clients; we typically recommend server-to-server calls for keys.
04:20 Sofia: Ok. If we want to run a small pilot next week, what do you need from us?
04:24 Marcus: Share sample prompts, target success metrics (e.g., NPS change, triage time reduction), and expected concurrency. With that, I can propose a minimal Dedicated config or advise hosted settings.
04:38 Priya: We'll share a 100-example prompt set and our success criteria.
04:44 Lena: Great. We'll also provide a step-by-step quickstart doc with code snippets for Node/Python and the free credit redemption link. Expect that in the follow-up email.
04:56 Tom: Do you have any benchmarks or perf numbers for long sequences? Our summarization may hit 1k tokens in, 1k tokens out-ish.
05:06 Marcus: We have public benchmarks but those are model-dependent. For long sequences optimization includes quantization, KV cache tuning, and batch sizing. For high throughput we recommend Dedicated with optimized kernels and pinned model versions. We'll run a short perf test if you want—send a representative file and we'll run it on hosted + dedicated to compare tail latencies.
05:27 Priya: That'd be helpful. Also, regarding data retention, can we configure log retention and exclude raw payloads from analytics?
05:34 Lena: Yes—on Hosted you can opt-out of analytics or redact tokens; Dedicated and Private give finer controls and can disable any collection.
05:44 Sofia: Any competitor comparison notes we should be aware of? We looked at Anthropic and OpenAI—what differentiates Redwood?
05:51 Lena: Customers come to Redwood for production-grade serving and predictable costs. We focus on runtime efficiency, deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private), and developer-first tooling like traceable rollouts and per-route cost insights. We also provide recommended batching/quantization configs via Redwood Optimize—though sometimes docs show up as Redwood Optima in quick notes, lol.
06:12 Tom: Haha. Noted. One more—do you have SDKs for mobile or edge?
06:17 Marcus: We have mobile-friendly examples but recommend server-side usage for keys. For edge inference we can discuss Private on-prem packaging.
06:26 Priya: Okay, let's recap next steps at the top-level?
06:30 Lena: Sure. Recap: 1) We'll send the quickstart guide and free credits link; 2) Marcus will draft a 2-week pilot config (hosted vs dedicated cost estimate); 3) EmberCare shares prompt set and success metrics; 4) Schedule a technical deep dive for Private deployments next Thursday 8/21.
06:47 Tom: That works.
06:50 Priya: Good. Thanks Lena and Marcus — excited to try the quickstart.
06:54 Lena: Thanks all. We'll email the next steps and docs.
06:58 (meeting ends)
